        FOUNDRY DISTRICT · THE ASH GUILD

        Rook, the Kiln Warden.

        Once the guild's furnace keeper, Rook now guards its abandoned works. His stone gauntlets channel pressure from the kiln floor; when the kiln overheats, the whole yard becomes his weapon.

        • Phase 1 / Pressure: boxing strings and a marked quake. Jump or leave the ring.
        • Phase 2 / Fracture: below 65% health, fault lines cut across the yard. Move sideways out of the strip.
        • Phase 3 / Overload: below 30%, furnace fans threaten a wider area. Circle behind him or use solid cover.

        Hit or grab him during a wind-up to interrupt it. After each special, punish the recovery. He can be thrown, knocked down and juggled. Your selected sparring difficulty controls damage and warning time.

        A single boss fight in the Foundry. Wave runs must finish before entering.

        COAT · COMBINE · RELEASE

        Turn a fighting style into a force of nature.

        A coating lasts 10 seconds and strengthens confirmed punches, kicks, weapon hits and throws. Coat or cast two different elements within six seconds to prime a fusion. Release it with 0 within eight seconds. Each new coating replaces your previous one.

        Movement / make your own opening.

        U jumps independently of attacks. Your movement direction steers in the air. Hold Q or Ctrl to duck under high hands and head kicks; body strikes and low attacks still reach you. Q keeps its grip-change and mount actions near a held or grounded opponent. Space plus a direction makes a backstep, sidestep or forward slip. In the air it evades once; a descending tap also arms a 0.18-second landing recovery. Time it just before the floor to regain control quickly without undoing damage. A missed early attempt cannot be repeated during that descent. The landing cue shows the timing.

        While airborne, B stretches a hand to the highlighted visible pillar or wall, then pulls you toward it. Aim with your movement direction. Press B again to detach or U to release with lift. The Anchor button also works from the ground. Cover blocks the cable and solid scenery stops your body. G spends 18 focus and 8 stamina for one wind redirect per flight, preserving a connected combo. Jump costs 8 stamina, anchors 12, and air evasion 12 outside infinite practice.

        Your controls.

        Choose a binding, then press a key. Conflicts swap places.

        Movement, powers and other bindings

        Keyboard / touch
        Standard gamepad: left stick moves · right stick aims · X punches · Y kicks · RB heavy · A jumps · B evades · LT guards · RT holds power · LB opens the element wheel · D-pad down grabs, right uses utility, left coats, up switches target · View / Back ducks or changes clinch grip · left stick click inflates · Start pauses. Button prompts below show your current keyboard bindings; written examples use the default keys.

        Coat · combine · release.

        Shift + 1 coats you in fire, Shift + 2 in lightning, Shift + 3 in stone and Shift + 4 in water. Coatings last ten seconds. Fire, lightning, earth and water increase melee damage by 25%, 18%, 22% and 12%, plus small flat bonuses. Coated hits spend two focus, or four on heavy attacks and throws. Earth resists 20% of incoming damage; water resists 12%. Coatings apply only to real damaging contacts. Their glow does not increase your reach. Fire ignites; water extinguishes fire and wets opponents; lightning conducts through wet bodies; earth turns wet marks into mud slows.

        Coat or cast two different elements within six seconds. A fusion remains ready for eight seconds; 0 releases it using normal combat startup and focus. Earth + fire makes lava, fire + water makes steam, water + lightning makes Thunder Tide, earth + water makes mud, fire + lightning makes plasma, earth + lightning makes Magnet quake, fire + wind makes Firestorm and water + wind makes Typhoon. Repeated casts of one element do not count as a mix. The Infuse buttons and the quick Release button work on mobile. Recipe cards reset free practice with the selected fusion ready.

        7 fires water, 8 lashes and pulls, 9 raises a waterspout cradle. The Elements bank has Earth, Fire and Water tabs with nine moves each. Tap More moves for the new techniques; Alt + 1–9 selects them on a keyboard. Alt+1 Crag uppercut, Alt+2 Ridge breaker and Alt+3 Quarry hammer; Alt+4 Cinder jab, Alt+5 Dragon breath and Alt+6 Phoenix dive; Alt+7 Current palm, Alt+8 Undertow ring and Alt+9 Waterwheel kick. Dragon breath stops when interrupted or cancelled into another move. The ridge travels along the ground and stops at solid cover. Stone fist, Blazing uppercut and Comet heel use the animated limb contacts. Flare rush and Tide step move continuously and stop at cover. Stone vault launches you from a grounded surface. A bubble releases when struck, grabbed or expired. Wet ground can extinguish flames; lava and charged pools remain visible and temporary. Easy combos + Element remix chooses water, earth, fire, lightning and existing hand-to-hand follow-ups.

        Cover, earth and fire / work the angle.

        Enter attaches to a nearby solid or leaves cover. WASD shuffles along it. Hold Q for an automatic peek: over a low barrier, or around the closest edge of a car. Tall cover requires moving to an edge first; hold [ or ] for a specific side. On mobile, hold Peek left, Pop up or Peek right while pressing an attack with another finger. Releasing peek ducks again and cancels a shot before it commits. Your actual exposed head and arms can be hit. Jump, evade or a melee attack leaves cover. Cars have separate body and cabin collision shapes. Destruction and fire pressure can force you out.

        1 raises a breakable earth wall for 12 seconds (maximum three). 2 launches a marked patch of ground into an air combo. 3 sweeps nearby grounded enemies with a seismic ring. 4 fires a travelling ember. 5 lays a short burning trail along a clear lane; enemies move out of it. 6 creates a close furnace burst. All six use shared focus and can queue between your existing attacks. Solid cover stops their path. Try 2 → J → K → L, or 4 → H → H → V → E. Learn cover, Cover duel and Earth / fire lab set up the new mechanics.

        Balance and power links / build an opening.

        Mix leg attacks, heavy strikes and environmental impacts to fill balance pressure. A break opens 1.8 seconds to start a throw with 22% extra damage. H, H → O → V → E links a wind lift, lightning, stretch catch and charged slam. While inflated, O charges your next rolling collision for 20 focus; J bursts into it, or L discharges a Thunder belly. The charge lasts six seconds. Follow-up buttons show specific actions for your current position and work directly in either control mode. Auto target keeps a reachable juggle and can choose a closer partner between attacks; turn it off for fixed manual selection.

        Weapon lab / combine the whole kit.

        Baton J alternates fast diagonal and return swings; L breaks guards and Z extends its arc. Staff J alternates thrust and sweep; I launches with a rising vault, L drops an overhead, and Z telescopes its reach. Pulse blaster J fires a travelling bolt, K kicks, L uses a close palm strike, and Z spends two rounds plus 20 wind on a lifting shot. N reloads six rounds; taking a hit or dropping the gun interrupts the reload. H still casts wind, E throws your weapon, V spring-throws it, and F drops it. Cover stops shots; a timed Shift parry reflects one, held guard reduces its damage, and dodges can avoid it. Aiming follows your selected target at wind-up; switch targeting off to fire along your facing. Easy combos reloads an empty blaster for you. Weapon lab buttons restore a passive practice setup. Weapons also lie around every arena.

        G / keep the power flowing.

        Gust step moves in your movement direction, or forward if you are standing still. It costs 18 wind and 8 stamina during finite practice or sparring. G can cancel a connected strike and preserves its combo; queue the next attack during the step. It cannot cancel a missed wind-up, throw, hold, or reload. Try J → G sideways → K, H → X → J → K, Z → H → X → Z → L, or X → Z → I → J → K → L in Manual. Tempest kick also has a direct button. The last L in the new mixed air routes stretches a heel into a rubber axe drop.

        A new place to find your flow.

        Switch between the Courtyard, Freight depot, Rooftop dojo, and Foundry above the arena. Bright discs are spring pads: step or roll onto one to launch, or knock a loose object across it. Swing bags keep their rope length and return with real momentum. Benches and wood dividers break under hard impacts. R restores the current arena. Center camera restores the starting view. Use Lean scenery on slower devices.

        Foundry / make a bigger chain reaction.

        Striped conveyor lanes carry grounded partners and loose cargo. Carts roll farther and resist lift; push them with wind, strikes, or balloon form. Carts are too heavy to carry. Amber vent grilles warn before a blue upward blast. Y near a striped control post cycles the belts forward, reverse, then off. The machinery button shows the current state. Turning off Springs & machinery disables belts, vents, pads, and powered rebound behavior. Glass screens block attacks until broken. Rebound pads send a knocked partner back into the air, ready for a follow-up. The open center stays available for ordinary combos.

        Environment trials / give the experiment a goal.

        Four trials set up glass, cargo, vent flight, and a rebound combo. Each has a 60-second clock and records a best time for your control mode on this browser. Goals count actual breaks and contacts. R or Retry restores the setup; Free play removes the clock and keeps the scene. Trials use normal speed with machinery active. Changing arena, mode, or combo assistance leaves the trial.

        Your input and your assisted move are different things.

        The PRESSED history shows your actual keys, including buffered taps. The action line may say K → ASSIST: GALE PALM when Easy combos uses wind for a distant air setup. K still registered as K. Manual keeps the original controls; moves can still change with the clinch, floor, air, equipped object, or a wind follow-up.

        Group lab / choose your own pressure.

        Practice against two or three opponents. Still targets wait, moving targets circle and defend, and live sparring lets one opponent attack at a time. T or the target cards chooses who your next move follows. The current strike stays aimed at its original target, so you can switch during a combo. Runners are light and fast; bruisers resist knockback; grapplers close into clinches; long-reach rivals stretch from distance. Gentle lowers damage to 40%, limits opponents to two attacks, and disables grabs and ground pressure. Easy starts at 62% damage and three attacks. Normal and Hard gradually add pressure. Health does not increase between rounds.

        Easy combos / find your rhythm without memorizing it.

        Choose Easy combos below the arena. Tap or hold J to chain a varied mix; K sets up a launch or continues an air combo, and L finishes. Combo flavor picks mixed fighting, wind and air, wrestling, or Power fusion. Power fusion links wind lifts, lightning, stretch catches and throws. Every tap requests one move; only two assisted moves queue ahead. Holding J keeps requesting moves until you release it. Movement, guarding, dodging, targets, stamina, and contact still matter. Throws and slams get room to land. The wind buttons cast a pull, dash, or cyclone directly in either control mode. Manual restores the original inputs and the full route library.

        H / Make the air part of the fight.

        In Manual, H → K draws a group toward you, and H → E rides a slipstream into a palm strike. A third H after an updraft creates a short cyclone that gathers bodies and loose props. L collapses it into a downburst. Use the direct wind buttons in either control mode. A cyclone has a fixed location, stops at cover, lasts under a second, and cannot stack with another cyclone from you. H sends a gale through a cone in front of you. H again calls an updraft at your aimed spot; H then L makes a downburst. H during an air combo sustains a juggle. Wind pushes loose props, swings bags, lifts clustered opponents, and stops at solid cover. Heavy enemies rise less and move less. Try H → H → H → L, H → K → E → K → E, or H → E → I → Z → X → L in Manual. Set up wind lab gathers three targets and a crate. Wind energy refills between casts; infinite stamina also gives infinite wind. H unrolls balloon form into wind.

        Seven partners. Different kinds of pressure.

        Choose a style under Partner & session, then switch to Sparring. Choose difficulty directly above the arena. Boxers pressure with hands; kickboxers keep kicking distance; wrestlers enter the clinch; elastic rivals work from range; scavengers pick up and throw objects. The Pulse rival starts with a blaster, keeps shooting distance, and reloads between magazines. The all-rounder mixes them. Opponents circle, retreat to recover stamina, and react after a visible wind-up. Tap Space repeatedly to spend stamina resisting an enemy’s clinch before their throw begins. The Footwork drill moves and defends without attacking. Practice speed slows the simulation so you can study transitions.

        C / Balloon bowling.

        C inflates your body and tucks your limbs in. Steer with WASD; momentum keeps you rolling after you release a direction. J spends pressure on a burst roll, Space or K bounces, L rises into a belly drop, and Shift brakes. Fast rolls bowl opponents over and fling loose props. Walls ricochet, heavy barrels return more force, and tables can break. Pressure refills between bursts. C or Q unrolls; H, I, E, Z, X, and V unroll directly into their normal attacks. Try bowling → I → J → K to switch back into an air combo. Set up bowling resets the courtyard with a clear run-up.

        The courtyard is part of your combo.

        F picks up chairs, crates, and barrels. With an object held: J swings, L hits harder, Z extends the swing, E throws, and V powers up the throw. K and I still kick and launch. F drops it so you can clinch again. B retrieves a distant object along a clear path. Objects wear down; tables and crates break under heavy impacts.

        Keep chaining through the throw.

        Queue up to four inputs during strikes or a lift. The timing bar shows your current move and waiting inputs. Throws deal damage on landing. J, K, and L follow up on the floor; Q moves to mount, E stands your opponent back up, and I pops them into the air. Button labels change with your position.

        Stretch controls: Z punch · X whip kick · V reel-in.

        Try Z → V → E for an elastic punch into a hip throw, or V → Q → Q → I for a stretching grab into a German suplex. V in a clinch performs a slingshot throw. Try Z → J → Z for a long straight, curved hook, and coiled double strike; X → X → X changes whip kick into low sweep and a high elastic arc. Use the Stretch tab to watch these from farther away.

        Mix your air and clinch attacks.

        I → J → J → J → K adds an aerial hook and flying knee. E → K → K → J → J → L releases the clinch with a shove; keep pressing J and K to return to boxing. V while airborne reels both fighters into a standing clinch.

        Make contact / find the opening.

        Gloves, feet and weapons must reach the moving body to land a hit. A high guard catches punches; low kicks can get underneath it. Cross an incoming swing with your weapon to clash. Step clear of a committed swing to make it miss.

        Feel both fighters react.

        Use the Combo / impact drill to see your own character take a full combination. Both fighters tumble, absorb floor impacts, and recover. The drill resets after a knockout.

        Try a German suplex: E → Q → Q → I.

        In sparring, grip control and stamina run down. Work quickly, change position, or release with Space.
